title: Flawed but Memorable: Student Critical Reception of Interest-Personalized GenAI Analogies in Computing Education
abstract: arXiv:2609.06095v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Motivation: Undergraduate computing students increasingly turn to generative AI (GenAI) tools to understand abstract concepts through analogies. Analogies compare an unfamiliar concept to something familiar, but judging whether the comparison holds requires knowledge of both. GenAI may also embed assumptions about who the learner is. GenAI education research centers on output correctness, leaving students' critical reception of analogies largely unexamined.   Method: We investigate how students evaluate the accuracy, appropriateness, and assumptions in GenAI-generated analogies, and their perceptions of interest-personalized versus generic technical explanations. Ten students with CS2 experience participated in a pre-survey, a think-aloud task with linked-list and recursion explanations, and a semi-structured interview grounded in the Paul-Elder framework. They judged accuracy, clarity, engagement, and trust separately.   Results: Most

translated_title: 有缺陷但令人难忘：计算教育中学生对兴趣个性化GenAI类比的批判性接受研究
translated_abstract: 动机：本科计算机专业学生越来越多地借助生成式AI（GenAI）工具，通过类比来理解抽象概念。类比是将不熟悉的概念与熟悉的事物进行比较，但判断这种比较是否成立需要对两者的了解。GenAI还可能嵌入关于学习者身份的假设。现有的GenAI教育研究主要聚焦于输出的正确性，而学生对类比的批判性接受度在很大程度上尚未被研究。方法：我们研究了学生如何评估GenAI生成类比的准确性、恰当性及其中的假设，以及他们对基于兴趣个性化的解释与通用技术解释的感知差异。十名具有CS2课程经验的学生参与了前测问卷、针对链表和递归解释的出声思维任务，以及基于Paul-Elder框架的半结构化访谈。他们分别评判了准确性、清晰度、吸引力和可信度。结果：大多数（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过出声思维任务和访谈发现，学生对GenAI生成的兴趣个性化类比能够进行批判性评估，识别其中的不准确之处和隐含假设，但这些有缺陷的个性化类比因贴合学生兴趣反而更令人难忘。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that while students critically evaluate interest-personalized GenAI analogies—identifying their inaccuracies and embedded assumptions—these flawed yet personalized analogies prove more memorable to learners in computing education.
